en: The Sūtra on Praising the Pure Land and Being Sustained by the Buddha, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove.
At the Anāthapiṇḍada Monastery, he was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus;
all were venerable elder śrāvakas of renowned reputation and great arhats, headed by such great śrāvakas as the Venerable Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, and Aniruddha.

Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all of whom dwelt in the stage of non-retrogression and were adorned with a multitude of immeasurable merits. Their names were:
the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Aparājita, the Bodhisattva Nityodyukta, and the Bodhisattva Anikṣiptadhura; these and other great bodhisattvas served as his leaders.

Furthermore, Śakra, the Great Brahmā King, the Lord of the Sahā World, the Four World-Protecting Kings, and a multitude of tens of billions of celestial sons led by these foremost figures, as well as immeasurable others from the world—gods, humans, asuras, and so forth—all came together to this assembly to hear the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra: "Do you know this?
To the west of this world, beyond hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayuta buddha-fields, there is a buddha-world named Sukhāvatī."

Among them, the World-Honored One is named Amitāyus and Amitābha, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfected in the ten titles; he currently dwells there in peace and stability, proclaiming the profound and subtle Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, enabling them to attain supreme benefit and happiness.
“Furthermore, Śāriputra!
For what cause and for what reason is that Buddha-world named ‘Supreme Bliss’ (Sukhāvatī)? Śāriputra!”

Because within that realm, none of the sentient beings experience any physical or mental sorrow or suffering, but instead possess only immeasurable, pure joy and bliss, it is therefore called the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Throughout the pure buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, there are everywhere sevenfold rows of exquisite jeweled railings, sevenfold rows of precious tāla trees, and sevenfold nets of exquisite jewels surrounding it on all sides, adorned with the four treasures—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal—interlaced in wondrous patterns."

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there are such various exquisite adornments and magnificent arrays of merit, so exceedingly delightful that it is therefore called the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Throughout the Pure Buddha-land of Sukhāvatī, there are everywhere ponds made of the seven wonderful jewels, filled to the brim with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities."
What are the eight qualities of the water? First, it is limpid and pure; second, it is cool and refreshing;

third, it is sweet and delicious; fourth, it is light and soft; fifth, it is moistening and lustrous; sixth, it is tranquil and harmonious; seventh, when drunk, it eliminates immeasurable afflictions such as hunger and thirst; eighth, after drinking, it is certainly able to nourish the sense faculties and the four great elements.
It increases various kinds of superior roots of goodness, and sentient beings with abundant merit always joyfully enjoy its use.
The bottoms of these jewel ponds are strewn with golden sand, and on all four sides there are four stairways adorned with the four precious substances, which are most delightful.
Surrounding the ponds are rows of exquisite jewel trees, interspersed and arranged so that their fragrances waft abroad; adorned with the seven treasures, they are exceedingly lovely.
As for the seven treasures, they are: first, gold; second, silver; third, vaidūrya; fourth, sphaṭika; fifth, red pearl; sixth, aśmagarbha; and seventh, musāragalva.

In these various ponds, there are always lotus flowers of diverse colors, as large as chariot wheels: blue in form, blue in appearance, blue in light, and blue in shadow; yellow in form, yellow in appearance, yellow in light, and yellow in shadow; red in form, red in appearance, red in light, and red in shadow; white in form, white in appearance, white in light, and white in shadow; and fourfold in form, fourfold in appearance, fourfold in light, and fourfold in shadow.

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there are such various exquisite adornments, and its meritorious ornaments are so exceedingly delightful that it is therefore named the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the pure buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, there are always spontaneously present immeasurable and boundless varieties of exquisite music, with melodies that are harmonious, elegant, and most delightful."

When all classes of sentient beings hear this sublime sound, all their evil afflictions are completely extinguished, immeasurable wholesome dharmas gradually increase, and they swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there are such various exquisite adornments and magnificent arrays of merit, so exceedingly delightful, that it is therefore called the World-Sphere of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the Pure Buddha-land of Sukhāvatī, the entire ground is composed of pure gold; its touch is soft and supple, it is fragrant, clean, and radiant, and it is interspersed with immeasurable and boundless exquisite jewels."

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there are such various exquisite ornaments and adornments of merit, so exceedingly lovely and delightful, that it is therefore named the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the pure buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, throughout the six periods of day and night, various kinds of exquisite celestial flowers rain down constantly—glossy, fragrant, and pure, fine, soft, and multicolored. While they cause those who see them to experience physical and mental bliss, they do not give rise to craving or attachment, and they increase the immeasurable, incalculable, and inconceivable, most excellent merits of sentient beings."
Those sentient beings constantly offer worship to Amitāyus Buddha during the six periods of day and night.

Every morning, carrying these celestial flowers, they fly for the duration of a single meal to immeasurable worlds in other directions to make offerings to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Buddhas. At each of those Buddhas' abodes, they scatter hundreds of thousands of koṭis of tree-flowers as an offering, then return to their original location to roam among the heavens and dwell there.

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there are such various wondrous and exquisite adornments, with the splendor of its merits so exceedingly delightful that it is therefore named the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In the pure buddha-field of the World of Ultimate Bliss, there are always various kinds of wondrous, lovely, and multicolored birds, namely:
geese, wild ducks, sarus cranes, egrets, swans, cranes, peacocks, parrots, kalaviṅkas, and jīvañjīvakas."

In this way, these various birds constantly assemble together during the six periods of day and night, producing harmonious and elegant sounds; according to their respective species, they proclaim the wondrous Dharma, namely:
the profound foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of psychic power, faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment, the limbs of the path, and other such immeasurable sublime teachings.

When the sentient beings of that land hear this sound, each of them attains the immeasurable merit of mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, and mindfulness of the Sangha, which perfumes and cultivates their bodies. Śāriputra, what do you think?
Could those birds in that land possibly be included among the animals of the evil destinies?
Do not hold such a view. Why is this?
In that Buddha’s Pure Land, there are no three evil realms; even the names of the three evil destinies are not heard, let alone the actual animals (tiryag-yoni) summoned by sinful karma!
You birds should know that all of you are emanations created by the Buddha Amitāyus, sent to proclaim the sounds of immeasurable Dharma and to bring benefit and peace to all sentient beings.

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there are such various exquisite adornments, and its meritorious decorations are so exceedingly delightful that it is therefore called the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In the pure buddha-field of the World of Ultimate Bliss, there is always a wondrous wind that blows through the various jeweled trees and jeweled nets, producing subtle and sublime sounds."
For example, it is like hundreds of thousands of koṭis of celestial musical instruments playing simultaneously, producing subtle and exquisite sounds most worthy of appreciation;

likewise, in that land, there is always a wondrous wind that blows through the various jewel trees and jeweled nets, striking them to produce all manner of subtle and exquisite sounds that proclaim various Dharmas.
When the sentient beings of that land hear this sound, they give rise to immeasurable merits such as the mental application of mindfulness toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Śāriputra,

because that buddha-field possesses such wondrous and exquisite adornments, and its meritorious decorations are so exceedingly delightful, it is therefore named the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
within the pure buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, there are such immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and most rare occurrences as these."

Even if one were to pass through hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas, using hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of tongues, with each tongue producing immeasurable sounds to praise its merits, one could never reach the end; for this reason, it is called the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
“Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In the pure buddha-field of the World of Ultimate Bliss, for what reason is the Buddha named Amitāyus? Śāriputra!”
Because that Tathāgata and all sentient beings therein have lifespans of immeasurable and incalculable great kalpas,
for this reason, the Tathāgata of that land is named Amitāyus (Immeasurable Life).
Śāriputra! It has been ten great kalpas since the Buddha Amitāyus realized anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Śāriputra!
For what reason is that Buddha named Immeasurable Light?

Śāriputra, it is because that Tathāgata constantly emits immeasurable and boundless sublime light, which universally illumines all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions, performing the work of a Buddha without any obstruction.
For this reason, the Tathāgata of that land is named Immeasurable Light.
Śāriputra! Because that Buddha’s pure land has achieved such magnificent adornments of merit and is exceedingly delightful, it is called the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the Pure Buddha-land of Sukhāvatī, the Buddha Amitāyus constantly has immeasurable śrāvaka disciples; all of them are great arhats, fully endowed with various subtle and wondrous merits, the measure of which is boundless and beyond calculation."
Śāriputra! That Buddha’s pure land is adorned with such accomplished merits that it is exceedingly delightful; therefore, it is named the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the pure buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, the Buddha Amitāyus always has immeasurable bodhisattva disciples, all of whom are bound to only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*). They are endowed with various subtle and wondrous merits, the measure of which is boundless and incalculable; even if one were to praise their merits for an immeasurable number of kalpas, one could never reach the end."
Śāriputra! Because that buddha-field is adorned with such perfected merits and is exceedingly delightful, it is therefore named the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

All sentient beings who are born in that land are non-retrogressive; they shall certainly never again fall into the various perilous evil realms, nor into the borderlands, the lowly classes, or among the mlecchas. They will constantly roam through the pure lands of the Buddhas, and their sublime practices and vows will increase with every thought-moment, until they are certain to realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
Śāriputra! Because that buddha-field is adorned with such accomplished merits and is exceedingly delightful, it is therefore named the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
If sentient beings hear of that western pure buddha-field of the Buddha Amitāyus, adorned with immeasurable merits, they should all resolve to be born in that buddha-field."

Why is this? Because if one is born in that land, one will join the same assembly as such great beings adorned with immeasurable merit; one will enjoy such a pure Buddha-land adorned with immeasurable merit; one will never regress from the joy of the Mahāyāna Dharma; and one’s immeasurable practices and vows will increase in every thought-moment, swiftly realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Therefore, Śāriputra, the sentient beings born in that buddha-field have accomplished immeasurable and boundless merit; sentient beings who possess only meager roots of virtue shall not attain rebirth in the pure buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, the World of Immeasurable Life.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If there are sons or daughters of good family with pure faith who hear the names of the Immeasurable Life Buddha’s immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable merits, as well as the meritorious adornments of the World of Ultimate Bliss, and having heard them, reflect upon them for one day and night, or two, three, four, five, six, or seven days and nights, maintaining focused mindfulness without distraction."

When these good sons or good daughters approach the end of their lives, Amitāyus Buddha, together with his immeasurable assembly of śrāvaka disciples and bodhisattvas, will surround them from front and back and appear before them. Bestowing the grace of compassion, he will cause their minds not to become distracted;
once they have passed away, they will follow the Buddha’s assembly and be reborn in the pure buddha-field of the Land of Utmost Bliss, where Amitāyus dwells.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Observing such great causes and conditions for benefit and peace, I speak these words of truth.

If there are sons or daughters of good family with pure faith who hear of the inconceivable merit of the name of this Buddha Amitāyus and of the Pure Buddha-land of Sukhāvatī, they should all believe and accept it, make a vow, and practice as taught, so as to be born in that Buddha-land."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Just as I now extol and praise the immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable merits of the Buddha-field of the Buddha Amitāyus, so too in the eastern direction there are the present Tathāgatas Acala, Merudhvaja, Mahāmeru, Meruprabhāsa, and Citradhvaja.

Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reside in the eastern direction. From their respective pure lands, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak words of truth: "
"You sentient beings should all believe and accept this Dharma-gate of the inconceivable merits of the Buddha-fields, as thus praised, which is embraced by all Buddhas."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the southern direction there are also present the Tathāgatas Sūryacandraprabha, Yaśaḥprabha, Mahārciskandha, Meruprabha, and Anantavīrya. Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā, reside in the south. From their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, covering the entire trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak these words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all with faith accept this Dharma-gate of inconceivable praise for the merits of the buddha-fields, which is embraced by all Buddhas.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the western direction there are also present Buddhas such as Amitāyus Tathāgata, Amitaskandha Tathāgata, Amitaprabha Tathāgata, Amitadhvaja Tathāgata, Maheśvara Tathāgata, Mahāprabha Tathāgata, Arciṣmat Tathāgata, Mahāratnadhvaja Tathāgata, and Raśmipramokṣa Tathāgata. Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reside in the western direction. From their respective pure lands, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak these words of truth:
'All you sentient beings should with faith accept this Dharma-gate of the inconceivable merits of the Buddha-fields, praised by all Buddhas and embraced by them.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the northern direction there are currently the Tathāgatas Immeasurable Radiance Adorned Penetrating Awakened Wisdom, Immeasurable Celestial Drum Resounding Great Sublime Sound, Great Aggregate, Light Net, and Sāla King. Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reside in the north. From their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak these words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all with faith accept this Dharma-gate of the inconceivable merits of the buddha-fields, praised by all Buddhas and embraced by them.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the direction below, there are present Tathāgatas who manifest all the sublime Dharma and the principles of correct reasoning, constantly emitting the supreme light of the Victorious King of Fire: Tathāgata Śrīguṇaprabha, Tathāgata Siṃha, Tathāgata Yaśas, Tathāgata Kīrtiprabha, Tathāgata Saddharma, Tathāgata Sudharma, Tathāgata Dharmadhvaja, Tathāgata Guṇamitra, and Tathāgata Guṇakīrti. Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reside in the direction below. From their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak these words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all with faith accept this Dharma-gate of the inconceivable merits of the buddha-fields, which is praised by all Buddhas and embraced by them.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the zenith there are also present Tathāgatas such as Brahmaghoṣa, Nakṣatrarāja, Gandhaprabha, Padmottaraśrī, and Sarvārthadarśin. Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reside in the zenith; from their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the broad and long tongue-mark, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all believe and accept this Dharma-gate of inconceivable praise for the merits of the buddha-fields, which is embraced by all Buddhas.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the southeastern direction there is the present Tathāgata Supreme and Vast Cloud-Thunder-Sound King. Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā, reside in the southeastern direction. From their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all believe and accept this Dharma-gate of the inconceivable merits of the buddha-fields, which is praised by all Buddhas and embraced by them.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the southwestern direction there is the present Tathāgata named Supreme Sunlight Renown and Merit. Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reside in the southwestern direction. From their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak these words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all believe and accept this Dharma-gate of the inconceivable merits of the buddha-fields, praised by all Buddhas and embraced by them.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the northwest there is the present Tathāgata Immeasurable Virtue Fire-King Radiance (*Anantaguṇāgnirāja-prabhāsa*). Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, dwell in the northwest; from their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak these words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all believe and accept this Dharma-gate of inconceivable praise for the virtues of the buddha-fields, which is embraced by all Buddhas.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Likewise, in the northeast there are currently countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Tathāgatas of Vast Wisdom. Such Buddhas as these, as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā, dwell in the northeast; from their respective pure buddha-fields, each manifests the mark of the broad and long tongue, completely covering the trichiliocosm and surrounding it on all sides, as they speak words of truth:
'You sentient beings should all with faith accept this Dharma-door of the inconceivable merits of the buddha-fields, praised by all Buddhas and embraced by them.'"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, for what reason is this sutra titled 'The Dharma Gate of Praising the Inconceivable Merits of Buddha-fields and Being Sustained by All Buddhas'?"

Śāriputra! Because this sutra extols and praises the inconceivable merits of the Buddha-field of Amitāyus in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and because the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the ten directions—desiring through skillful means to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings—each remain in their own lands, manifest great spiritual transformations, and speak words of truth to exhort sentient beings to believe and accept this Dharma, this sutra is therefore titled "The Dharma Door of Praising the Inconceivable Merits of the Buddha-fields and Being Upheld by All Buddhas."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family—whether they have already heard it, will hear it in the future, or are hearing it now—upon hearing this sutra, gives rise to profound faith and understanding;
having given rise to faith and understanding, they will certainly be sustained by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who reside in the ten directions throughout ten Ganges-sands of worlds."

Those who practice as they have been taught will all certainly attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and all shall be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Utmost Bliss of the Buddha Amitāyus.

Therefore, Śāriputra! All you sentient beings should with faith accept and understand the words of myself and the World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions; you should apply yourselves with diligent effort, practice according to what has been taught, and harbor no doubts.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family has already made a vow, will make a vow, or is now making a vow regarding the meritorious adornments of the pure Buddha-field of the immeasurable life of the World of Ultimate Bliss, they shall certainly be sustained by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who reside in the ten directions—ten Ganges-sands in number.

Those who practice according to what they have said will all certainly attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and all will certainly be born in the pure Buddha-field of the World of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha Immeasurable Life."

Therefore, Śāriputra, any son or daughter of good family who possesses pure faith should all, with a profound heart of faith and understanding, resolve to be reborn in the pure Buddha-land of the Infinite Life World of Ultimate Bliss, and must not practice negligence.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Just as I now extol and praise the inconceivable merits of the Buddha-field of Amitāyus in the world of Sukhāvatī,
so too do the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the ten directions praise my own inconceivable and boundless merits, all saying these words:"
"How most marvelous and rare!

Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Hero, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One—how you are able, within this Sahā world during the five corruptions of the evil age, namely:

the corruption of the kalpa, the corruption of sentient beings, the corruption of afflictions, the corruption of views, and the corruption of lifespan—to realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi therein, and for the sake of skillfully benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings, to proclaim this Dharma which is most difficult for the world to believe."

"Therefore, Śāriputra, you should know that it is for the sake of skillfully benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings that I have now realized anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in this defiled world of the five corruptions during this evil age; thus I proclaim this teaching which is extremely difficult for the world to believe, which is most rare, and inconceivable."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In this world-system of defilement during the evil age of the five corruptions, if there are sons or daughters of good family with pure faith who, upon hearing such teachings as these—which are extremely difficult for the world to believe—can give rise to faith and understanding, receive and uphold them, proclaim them, and practice according to the instructions."
One should know that such a person is truly rare, having planted roots of goodness under immeasurable Buddhas in the past.

At the end of this life, they will certainly be reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, where they will enjoy the Mahāyāna Dharma-joy adorned with various merits and purities. Six times each day and night, they will personally approach and make offerings to Amitāyus Buddha, traveling through the ten directions to make offerings to all Buddhas. In the presence of these Buddhas, they will hear the Dharma and receive predictions of enlightenment; thus, their provisions of merit and wisdom will swiftly reach fulfillment, and they will quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
When the Blessed One had finished speaking this sutra,

the Venerable Śāriputra and the other great śrāvakas, as well as the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the vast multitude of devas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
The Sūtra on Praising the Pure Land and Being Received by the Buddha.
